newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. group seeks resolution of Manila telecom row.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group seeks resolution of Manila telecom row.

text.p: The American Chamber of Commerce in the Philippines said on Tuesday the government should take quick and decisive steps to facilitate the interconnection of all telecommunication carriers in the country.

Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT), which used to be a monopoly until the government opened the telecommunications sector recently, has been locked in a dispute with its new rivals who say it has dithered on the interconnections in a bid to keep them out.

"Sucessful telecommunications development depends on efficient interconnection of all carriers to form a seamless national telecommunications network. Failure to create this network in the Philippines would mean this country losing comparative advantage with other possible investment locations," the chamber said in its position paper.
PLDT had said it would need investment of $50.81 million to fully interconnect with other local operators.
Two weeks ago, the National Telecommunications Commission asked PLDT to ensure full interconnection with its competitors.
PLDT denied it was delaying the interconnections. Senior vice president Antonio Samson said PLDT has always been up to date in its interconnection agreements with other carriers.
